items.title: The most recent review searched only to March 2022
items.whyItMatters: Studies of text messages and targeted outreach published since then are missing from the only synthesis (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Update the search from January 2022, overlapping the review's end date, and add its included studies.

items.title: Timing evidence is confounded
items.whyItMatters: The only direct comparison of two and six weeks compared two different hospices (claim c2), yet colleagues want to move the call earlier.
items.opportunity: Extract timing as reported with the design, and state that the direction is uncertain.

items.title: Uptake is defined in different ways
items.whyItMatters: Accepting an offer and attending a session are different outcomes and cannot be compared as one number.
items.opportunity: Fix accepting an offer and attending at least one session as two separately extracted definitions.

items.title: Groups who rarely take up support are barely studied
items.whyItMatters: Men, relatives who need an interpreter and relatives living far away have the lowest uptake (claim c4), and no retrieved study tested outreach adapted for them.
items.opportunity: Extract results by sex, language and distance wherever reported and report their absence as a finding.

items.title: Rapid review shortcuts can miss studies
items.whyItMatters: Single-reviewer screening and an English-language limit can omit relevant service evaluations.
items.opportunity: Verify a random 20 percent of screening decisions and report every shortcut with its likely effect.

errorsFound: The need assumes an earlier first call would raise uptake; the retrieved comparison favoured six weeks over two weeks, although site differences confound it.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a rapid review that updates the 2023 synthesis, keeps two uptake definitions apart, extracts results for the groups with the lowest uptake, and reports its shortcuts openly.
summary: Five gaps: an out-of-date synthesis, confounded timing evidence, inconsistent outcome definitions, understudied groups, and shortcut bias.
